SUMMARY SHEET

**CLASS NAME:**   Problem Solving through Programming  
**TEACHER:**          Zach Stanfill

**CLASS DESCRIPTION:** 

This course offers a unique deep dive into the world of problem-solving through the lens of programming. Over the semester, we'll tackle a few problems, which allows us to dedicate two weeks to each. You'll learn to dissect challenges, design solutions, and bring them to life using code and principles. Having the option to use modern programming languages or graphical coding tools to craft our solutions, we will explore different programming paradigms and discover the tools that best suit your style. We'll begin by mastering fundamental programming concepts, then transition to dissecting each problem with flowcharts and pseudocode. From simple mathematical calculators to data manipulation and automation, you'll gain practical experience in programming.

This isn't just about learning to code; it's about cultivating critical thinking and logical reasoning. You'll develop the skills to approach any challenge with a structured, analytical mindset – skills that extend far beyond the computer screen. Team up with your classmates, don't be afraid to make mistakes, and high-five each other when you crack the code\! This course is all about building a problem-solving toolkit that will help you tackle challenges in school and life. Get ready to think in new ways, see problems from different angles, and discover the creative problem solver inside you.

This course is designed for anyone in the 8-12 grade level with any level of computer or programming experience. Although we will be coding, don’t shy away due to lack of experience, we will have plenty of resources explaining coding basics and join up in groups for some extra reinforcement with any troublesome points.

**CLASS OBJECTIVES:**

* How to Approach Solution Development

* Developing Solution Workflows

* Pseudo Coding Solution

* Coding the Solution

* Testing and Group Review

**STUDENT SAFETY DISCLAIMER:**

We understand that internet safety is a top priority for parents. In this Introduction to Programming course, we take that concern seriously. Rest assured that students will not have any access to the internet during class time. All coding activities will be conducted on a secure, closed network using HSE-issued laptops. This controlled environment ensures that students can focus on learning programming fundamentals without external distractions or exposure to potentially inappropriate content.

Our curriculum is designed to be self-contained, with all necessary resources and materials provided within the closed network. This approach allows us to maintain a safe and focused learning environment while still providing students with the hands-on experience and tools they need to develop their programming skills. We believe this balance between security and educational opportunity is essential for a successful learning experience.

Any and all questions regarding your student’s safety are welcomed and will be answered promptly.

2024 FALL SEMESTER 

WEEK 1: Class Introductions, Class Overview, Programming Overview, HelloWorld Application

WEEK 2: Introduction to Problem Solving Process, Brief Overview of Programming Basics (Variables, Data Types,  Operations, Conditionals, Looping, and Algorithms)

WEEK 3 \- 4:      Problem \- Finding the Max Number

WEEK 5 \- 6:      Problem \- Simple Calculator (Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, Division)

WEEK 7 \- 8:      Problem \- Roman Numeral to Modern Numbers

WEEK 9 \- 10:    Problem \- Sorting a List of Numbers

WEEK 11 \- 12:  Problem \- Calculating the Fibonacci Sequence

WEEK 1: This week is all about getting to know each other and the exciting journey we're about to embark on. We'll kick things off with introductions and a fun icebreaker to get comfortable in our new coding community. Then, we'll dive into the course overview, exploring the awesome problems we'll tackle and the different programming languages you'll get to play with.

Next, we'll take our first steps into the world of programming\! We'll discuss what programming is all about and why it's such a valuable skill to have. Finally, we'll get our hands dirty with our very first program – the classic "Hello, World\!" You'll learn how to write this simple program in one of the languages offered in the course, and we'll celebrate our first coding victory together\!

WEEKLY OBJECTIVE:

* Learn about each other (Teachers and Students)

* Learn about our development and coding environments

* Run our first “Hello World” program

* Go over class handouts

SUPPLY AND ROOM NEEDS  
       	SPRING 2025 SEMESTER

CLASS NAME: Problem Solving through Programming  
TEACHER: Zach Stanfill

WEEK 2: This week, we'll unlock the secrets of how programmers tackle problems. We'll explore the problem-solving process, learning how to break down complex challenges into smaller, more manageable steps. Get ready to map out solutions using flowcharts and pseudocode – your secret weapons for designing elegant and effective programs.

But that's not all\! We'll also dive into the building blocks of programming. You'll discover the power of variables to store information, learn about different data types (like numbers and text), and explore how operations and conditionals give your programs the ability to make decisions. And don't forget about loops – they'll help you automate repetitive tasks and make your code super efficient. By the end of the week, you'll be thinking like a true programmer, ready to tackle real-world problems with code\!

WEEKLY OBJECTIVE:  

* How to break down our problem

* How to design a solution flowchart

* How to write a pseudocode solution 

* Coding Fundamentals
